correctness.rationale: Proved via an exact finite-index decomposition for pairwise centered Hilbert features and explicitly computed one- and two-variable polynomial integrals. The key mixed contraction equals 13/1260, the mean-mode contraction equals 1/126, and their difference 1/420. Diagonal moment calculations and variance contractions give all six rational expressions. Derivative factorizations prove strict all-n correlation monotonicity and ordering. Standard-library checker independently verified all polynomial identities and 13,510 checks, while the all-integer proof uses the displayed formulas rather than finite numerical tests. n=1 Watson zero variance excluded from correlation.

originality.rationale: The 2021 primary source defines the characterization statistic and derives limiting single-test cumulants, not the exact finite-sample covariance of its weighted-indicator kernel with classical EDF tests. The 2024 integrated-empirical-process paper covers classical and generalized EDF tests but not that specific cross-kernel. published-finding corpus searches returned nearest results for pairs of classical EDF tests and unrelated same-sample covariances, none containing the characterization feature f_t or the rank-one share. The new exact joint contractions, sample-size monotonicity and a universal 10/13 mean-mode bound are not implied by those inspected statements without additional computations. Historical uniqueness is not asserted.
residual_risks: A broader historical paper on integrated weighted empirical processes may already have evaluated this particular cross-kernel without referencing its characterization-test name.
Searches and material inspected are finite; an unindexed source could imply the theorem. No independent audit of priority was performed.

value.rationale: The original 2021 paper directly compared practical performance of its omnibus statistic with Cramér–von Mises and Watson but did not quantify same-sample null dependence. The new exact all-size coupling provides a reproducible calibration ingredient for combined tests and identifies the structurally surprising dominance of the empirical-mean mode (strictly more than 10/13 of the total covariance) despite both tests being omnibus. It is one coherent motivated comparison, not arbitrary polynomial arithmetic. No power or independence claim is made.
